1385.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Swayye from the revered mouth of the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Primal Being, O Creator, you yourself are the cause of all creation. You fill everything, and pervade every heart. You are seen spread through the world; who knows your state? The Lord, the Master, himself protects all. You are imperishable and unmanifest, and came into being of yourself. You alone are, the One alone; there is no other like you. The Lord has no end, no near or far shore; who is there to reflect on (his bounds)? He is the father of the world, the support of all that breathe. (Guru) Nanak, the Lord's servant and devotee, is accepted at his door and is equal to God; what can one tongue tell (of him)? I am a sacrifice (to him), a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice. ॥1॥
Haan ki: a filler word of the refrain of these swayye, left unrendered.
1385.2: Streams of Amrit (the nectar of the Name) flow (from you), your treasures beyond weighing are full; you are beyond the beyond, boundless, infinite. You do as you will and take no other into your counsel; in your house creation and dissolution come about in a single blink. No other is your equal, your light is spotless; millions of sins depart by taking the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (Guru) Nanak, the Lord's servant and devotee, is accepted at his door and is equal to God; what can one tongue tell (of him)? I am a sacrifice (to him), a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice. ॥2॥
1385.3: He has set up all the worlds; from himself, the One, he has spread out the expanse; he pervades all, and yet is himself apart. O Lord, your virtues have no end or far shore; all beings and creatures are yours; O unknowable Murari (the Lord), you alone are the Giver of all. He himself holds up the creation and shows forth his power in it; he has no colour or mark, no mouth and no beard. (Guru) Nanak, the Lord's servant and devotee, is accepted at his door and is equal to God; what can one tongue tell (of him)? I am a sacrifice (to him), a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice. ॥3॥
1386.1: You are the treasure of all virtues; the worth of knowing you and meditating on you cannot be told; O God, your place is known to be the highest of the high. Mind, wealth and life are yours; the whole world is strung on your one thread; what likeness can I give you, greatest of the great? Who knows your secret, O unknowable, infinite, radiant Lord? O God, your power is whole and undivided; you are the support of all. (Guru) Nanak, the Lord's servant and devotee, is accepted at his door and is equal to God; what can one tongue tell (of him)? I am a sacrifice (to him), a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice. ॥4॥
1386.2: You are formless, and with form too; none can deceive you; you are all-pervading and imperishable; ever joyful, of endless forms, pure, and in full bloom. Countless beings sing your virtues, yet find not even a sesame seed's worth of your end. O God, the one to whom you are gracious, that person meets you. Blessed, blessed, blessed are those to whom the Lord, Har Har, has been gracious. Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, (one with) the Lord, are freed from both birth and death. ॥5॥
1386.3: The Lord is spoken of as True, True, True, True, true above all the true. There is no second, none other (like him); he is heard of as the Primal Being. Taking the Lord's Name, the Amrit, in the mind, every comfort is found. Those who have tasted it with the tongue are wholly satisfied and fulfilled. Those with whom the Master is well pleased love the Sat Sangat (the company of the true). Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, (one with) the Lord, have saved their whole lineage. ॥6॥
1386.4: His assembly is true, and true his court; he has placed the Truth with the True One (the Guru). He dwells on the true throne, and does true justice. The True One has created the world; he himself is beyond error, and never errs. His Name, a jewel, is infinite and priceless; its worth cannot be set. Those to whom Gobind (the Lord of the universe) has been gracious, they alone have found every comfort. Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, (one with) the Lord, do not come into births again. ॥7॥
1386.5: By what yoga, what knowledge, what meditation, in what way can he be praised? The Siddhas (yogis of perfect powers), the seekers and the thirty-three crore (gods) cannot find a particle of his worth. Brahma and the others, Sanak and his brothers, and Shesh Nag have not found the end of his virtues. The Ungraspable cannot be grasped; he fills all and is contained in all. Those whose noose the compassionate God has cut, they are the ones joined to his devotion. Those who have touched (the feet of) Guru Nanak, (one with) the Lord, are free for ever, here and hereafter. ॥8॥

Thirty-three crore (330 million): the number of the gods in Puranic tradition. Sanak and his brothers: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar, in the Puranas the four sons of Brahma, sages held to remain children for ever. Shesh Nag: the thousand-headed serpent of the Puranas, held to utter a new Name of God with every tongue.
1386.6: O God, O Giver, O Bountiful One, a beggar has fallen at your refuge; may (he) receive the gift of the dust of the Sants' feet, clinging to which the terrible world-ocean is crossed. I make a humble prayer; O Master, if it pleases you, hear my plea: grant me the sight of you, for my mind longs for it; may this mind be steadied in devotion. A lamp has been lit in the darkness; through the one Name, the true dharam, the whole Kalyug (the dark age) has been saved. O Lord, your servant Nanak, the Guru, (one with) the Supreme Lord, is manifest in all the world. ॥9॥
1387.1: Swayye from the revered mouth of the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (My) body is frail, and bound moreover by attachment; I am wicked, hard-hearted, unclean and ignorant. I run about and wander, and find no rest; I have not known the state of the Supreme Lord. Drunk with the wine of youth, beauty and Maya, I roam about distraught, and full of pride. Others' wealth, harsh words against others, (others') women, slander: these are sweet and dear to my heart. In hiding I contrive deceits; O God, Knower of hearts, you see and hear (it all). Gentleness, righteousness, compassion, purity: (in me) there are none; O Giver of life, I have come to your refuge. O all-powerful Cause of creation, O Siridhar (Master of Maya), O Master of Nanak, save (me). ॥1॥
1387.2: Singing the praise of the Enticer of the mind and taking his refuge are mighty warriors to destroy sins; the Lord is the boat that carries across, able in every way to save whole lineages. O heedless mind, remember (him), and come to know the Sat Sangat; beguiled by the darkness of doubt, where are you running? For an hour, a while, an instant, a moment, remember (him); take the Name of Ram with your tongue. (Worldly) work is shallow, its small pleasures are bonds; why wander in sorrow through millions of births? O Nanak, (taking) the Sants' teaching, meditate on the Name, and, dyed in the love of Ram, delight within your own self. ॥2॥
1387.3: From a drop of seed, in the field of the (mother's) body, (God) formed this rare human body and adorned it. (He gave) food and drink, mansions, and comforts to enjoy; cutting away distress, he took away (your) misfortune. All the understanding came (to you) to know mother, father, brothers and kin. Day by day you grow, and ever nearer comes dreadful old age. O worthless, wretched worm of Maya, remember the Master for (at least) a moment. O merciful Lord, treasure of mercy, take Nanak by the hand, and cut away (his) load of doubt. ॥3॥
1387.4: O mind, like a mouse in its hole you strut in pride, and do the deeds of a great fool. You sway back and forth on the swing of riches; lost in Maya, you wander like an owl. Sons, wife, friends, comforts and kin: your attachment to them has grown very great. You have sown the seed of ego, and its shoot is possessiveness; your life is passing in committing sins. Death, the cat, watches (you) with its mouth wide open; even as you enjoy your pleasures, you hunger with craving. O Nanak, in the Sat Sangat remember Gopal, the compassionate, knowing the world to be a dream. ॥4॥
1388.1: Neither body, nor house, nor love lasts for ever; O you drunk with Maya, how long will you be proud? Not the royal canopy, nor decrees, nor the whisk, nor those who wave it (will remain); (life) is flowing away, yet you do not reflect in your heart. Not chariots, nor horses, nor elephants, nor thrones (go with you); leaving them in an instant, you will depart naked. Not warriors, nor heroes, nor kings, nor chiefs: see with your own eyes, none of them goes with you. No fort, no shelter, no treasury brings release; doing evil, you go, shaking out both hands (empty). Not friends, nor sons, wife, kin and companions (stand by you); they turn away like the shade of a tree. Every moment remember God, the all-pervading Being, compassionate to the meek, beyond reach and infinite. O Master of Maya, O Lord, your servant Nanak is in your refuge; O Bhagvant, be gracious and carry (him) across. ॥5॥
The royal canopy (chhatar) is the sign of sovereignty; the whisk (chaur) is waved over one who is revered.
1388.2: Risking life, losing honour, taking alms, lying in wait on the roads, with love and all his attention, (man) gathers (wealth). From friends, kin, companions, sons and brothers he keeps it hidden away. Running here and there, practising falsehood: doing these, he has burnt away his body's span of life. Good deeds, righteousness, self-restraint, purity and vows: all these ways he has lost in the company of fickle (Maya). Beasts, birds, trees, things that do not move: through births of many kinds he has wandered, at great length. Not for an instant, a moment, a blink has he remembered the Name of the Master of the meek, the Lord of life, the Maker of all. Food and drink, sweet and savoury dishes, turn wholly bitter at the last hour. O Nanak, (those) attached to the Sants' feet are saved; all the others, sunk in Maya, have departed, leaving (everything) behind. ॥6॥
1388.3: Brahma and the others, Shiva, the Vedas and the great sages sing the Master's virtues, relishing them again and again. Indra, the chief of sages and Gorakh (the master of the yogis) search (for him); they come down to earth, then rush back to the skies. Siddhas, men, gods and demons find not a particle of his mystery. Through love for the beloved God, and devotion full of love's relish, the Lord's servants merge in the sight of him. Those who forsake him and beg from others, their mouths, teeth and tongues all wear away. O foolish mind, remember the Giver of peace; Nanak, the servant, counsels you. ॥7॥
1388.4: Maya plays in many colours; through doubt and attachment (the mortal) has fallen into a pitch-dark well. His pride is so great that the sky cannot hold it; (yet) his belly is filled with filth, bones and worms. He runs in the ten directions for the great poison (of Maya), snatches others' wealth, and is robbed by ignorance. His youth passes, the disease of old age seizes him; punished by Jam's messengers (the messengers of Death), he dies (a wretched) death. He suffers the agonies of many births, and the hells; under (Jam's) punishment he rots in a pit of pain. O Nanak, by loving devotion they are saved whom (the Lord) in his grace has himself made Sants. ॥8॥
1388.5: All virtues, and the fruits of all desires (are ours); our hope has been fulfilled. (The Lord's Name) is the medicine, the mantra and the charm that takes away others' pain, destroys every disease and brings about good. Lust, anger, pride, envy and craving perish when the Lord's Name is uttered. Holy bathing, charity, austerities, rites of purity: (in place of them all) we have enshrined God's lotus feet in the heart. The Lord is (our) friend, companion, comrade and kin; God is the sustenance of the soul and the support of life. We have taken the shelter of the all-powerful Master; Nanak, the servant, is ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥9॥
1389.1: One who has the relish of love for (the Lord's) lotus feet cannot be cut down by weapons; one whose mind is pierced on the path to (the Lord's) sight cannot be bound with a rope; one who stays clinging to the dust of (the Lord's) servants cannot be burnt by fire; water cannot drown those whose feet tread the Lord's path. O Nanak, (their) diseases, faults, sins and attachments are pierced through by the arrow of the Lord's Name. ॥1॥
1389.2: Many busy themselves with efforts of many kinds; many ponder the six Shastras (the schools of Hindu philosophy). Smeared with ashes, many wander to the places of pilgrimage; (some) waste the body thin, many tie up matted hair. Without worship of the Lord all of them suffer pain, like (the spider) that eagerly spins out its house of thread. (Some) perform worship, stamp (discus) marks (on the body), cook their own food (for purity); they put on shows of many kinds. ॥2॥
